## Wesley Stone

Hi! I'm a first-year MA Economics student at Duke University currently studying microeconomics, econometrics and game theory. My interests are broad — economics, ethics, politics, the rapid rise of AI — and in the past year I've done research on YIMBY housing policy, population ethics and global warming. Outside of work, I enjoy a good biography or historical fiction novel, playing guitar (electric and acoustic) and (very slowly) lowering my handicap on the golf course.

## Biography

I was born in Madison, Wisconsin, but I'd lived in Atlanta, Georgia nearly my entire life before returning to my Midwestern roots for college. I became interested in philosophy my first semester after taking an ethics class, and I soon decided to add data science to explore the foundations of the machine learning and artificial intelligence technology taking the world by storm. After studying abroad in Amsterdam junior spring, I spent my senior year immersed in research capstones for my two majors. For data science, I worked with a group to study the behavior of the Portland housing market after a statewide ban on exclusive single-family zoning. Our final paper is accessible on my website. And my philosophy capstone, entitled "A Risk-Sensitive Approach to Population Ethics," takes on the difficult question of determining a social welfare function to measure the value of populations of varying sizes and quality of life. I published this paper in the journal [Dianoia](https://ejournals.bc.edu/index.php/dianoia/index), and presented my findings at a conference at Boston College. This summer, I returned to my role as an analyst at Georgia Tech's Urban Climate Lab, contributing to critical research on warming trends in the biggest US cities. Now I'm beginning my career as a Blue Devil and diving deep into the world of economics, as well as beginning to construct a vision of what the future looks like for me.
